Headline: Which members are likely to renew
Story: Scores every member on how likely they are to renew, mostly from how long they have been a member and how recently they have engaged. A high score means the member looks like people who have renewed before.
DataStory: Trained on 1,840 members, about one in five of whom lapsed. Tenure carries most of the explanation; recent activity adds a meaningful amount on top of it. One input — the survey score — is missing for more than half of members, so it is used as a presence signal rather than a value.
BusinessConnection: Lets the team put its renewal outreach where it will matter: the members who look most at risk, rather than the whole list. A member scoring below 0.3 is worth a personal call.

Components.Headline: Membership tenure
Components.Story: How long this person has been a member, read from Members.MembershipTenureMonths. Longer-standing members renew more reliably, and this is the single strongest signal in the model.

Contribution.ReuseWhen: Any model about member loyalty or lifetime value, wherever a join date is recorded.

Components.Headline: Recent activity count
Components.Story: How many activities this member had in the year before the decision date, counted as-of that date so nothing from the future leaks in.

Contribution.ReuseWhen: Any model scoring member engagement where dated activity rows are available.

Caveats: The score reflects members who joined before 2026; a very new cohort may behave differently and should be watched.
It predicts likelihood, not certainty — a low score is a reason to reach out, not a conclusion that someone will leave.
Survey score is missing for most members, so the model is effectively blind to satisfaction.
